Capabilities are descriptive and do not grant execution or plugin authority.

missing_platform_primitives.blocked_until: No live model call or automatic selection before deterministic routing policy exists.

missing_platform_primitives.blocked_until: No hidden memory capture or broad indexing.

missing_platform_primitives.why_needed: Persistent assistants require explicit memory boundaries and source-truth precedence.

missing_platform_primitives.blocked_until: No browser/OAuth/tool bridge activation before a governed adapter contract and security audit.

missing_platform_primitives.blocked_until: No queue/autonomy/planner-builder execution before security gates.

missing_platform_primitives.blocked_until: No natural-language success claim should establish action success.

missing_platform_primitives.why_needed: Persistent agents need a visible way to stop, revoke, quarantine, and audit them.

missing_platform_primitives.blocked_until: Suspicion must fail closed and surface to Guardian/Chief.
missing_platform_primitives.why_needed: Agent platforms need a deterministic way to classify suspicious behavior, stale receipts, and unexpected capability requests.

operator_summary: OpenClaw already has many agent-platform primitives as deterministic contracts: packages, capabilities, gates, receipts, awareness maps, stable app map transport, and health proof. It does not yet have live persistent agents. The next safe step is to define agent identities and actor/model routing before any package dispatch or tool authority.
